summary:
Elk is a web client for Mastodon. I saved 5 views, but only from the signed-out, public side of the app: signing in failed. Clicking "Sign in" showed a "Cannot connect to the server." error both times I tried, so the app stayed in "Viewing localhost:4410 public data" mode.

Saved views (each replays and matches the original screen):
1. explore-posts (/explore): the trending posts tab, with tabs across the top, posts with image and link cards, action bars and the instance sidebar.
2. profile (/@maren): a profile page with banner, avatar, bio, metadata fields, follower counts, tabs and pinned posts.
3. thread (opened by clicking the "Thank you!" post in /public/local): a single post with the posts it replies to shown above it.
4. explore-news (/explore/links): trending news as a list of link cards.
5. settings-interface (/settings/interface): a two-pane settings screen with font size, color mode, theme color and bottom-navigation options.

Not reached because they need a signed-in account: the Home timeline (/home sends you to /public/local), Notifications, Conversations, Favourites, Bookmarks, Lists, Hashtags, Scheduled posts and the compose box. I skipped the Local/Federated timelines because they use the same post-list layout as the Explore posts tab.
